query: What signals suggest an expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the asset from short_description/ci, giving a groundable axis to group decline rates by asset type. Reasonably useful though indirectly tied to decline; values well-supported by source text.

per_column.name: asset_purpose_scope
per_column.rationale: Purpose classification is largely redundant with asset_category_type (service->cloud_service, laptop->general_business track together) and some assignments (e.g. iPod touch -> cloud_service) are loose inferences. Moderate leverage.

per_column.name: asset_brand_vendor
per_column.rationale: Vendor extraction from ci/description is a plausible new grouping axis (vendor-linked decline patterns) and mostly well-grounded, though 'cloud_provider' for a service is inferred rather than stated.

per_column.name: processing_lag_indicator
per_column.rationale: Lag between opened_at and processed_date is a strong candidate signal for decline; derivable from date columns. NULL/Unknown for nan processed_date is correct behaviour.

per_column.name: department_origin
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing 'department' column, and samples show values (sales, customer_support, product_management) with no supporting cue in the provided source text, suggesting invented assignment rather than grounded reading.

per_column.name: source_id_validity
per_column.rationale: Presence/absence of source_id is a plausible decline signal (missing identifiers -> rejection) and directly derivable from the source_id column.

per_column.name: asset_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Vague vs specific description is a reasonable decline signal (vague expenses more likely rejected) and grounded in the description text, though specific/generic boundary is somewhat subjective.

per_column.name: travel_associated_flag
per_column.rationale: Binary travel flag derivable from category/description; a plausible grouping axis for policy-driven declines, though somewhat narrow and overlapping with category.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine axes relevant to predicting declines (processing lag, source_id validity, specificity, travel), and their values are largely sound readings of the source text. Weak points: asset_purpose_scope duplicates asset_category_type, and department_origin both duplicates an existing original column and shows ungrounded, seemingly invented values in the samples. Overall the set offers real analytical leverage with mostly well-grounded values.
